The engine/chassis and suspension sheets were visually read; their original publication/date is not established. Published 280 bhp net is distinct from the club history’s 300 bhp. Torque is explicitly gross. No conversion, test speed or acceleration is inferred. The 1960 steel-bodied Gordon GT prototype, later I.T. naming, modifications and de Bruyne projects do not create extra counts.
cars.summary: The Gordon-Keeble combined a Chevrolet V8 with a tubular spaceframe, de Dion rear suspension and four-wheel disc brakes in a practical four-seat GT. This ambitious Anglo-American performance design has a documented place in specialist British sports-car history. The production car earns one family entry for its engineering and sporting purpose, rather than rarity alone.

cars.specification_market: 1953 Vignale road-coupe collection/archive reference. Native displacement and supported architecture retained. The archive table’s 310 hp and optional Torqueflite statement are not imported: power differs across published accounts and the transmission label raises a chronology problem. No gearbox, speed, acceleration, production total or modern net/gross standard is asserted. C-1/C-2R/C-4R race specifications, the earlier American-bodied C3 and modern continuations do not transfer into this reference.
cars.summary: The C3 brought Cunningham’s American V8 sports-car project to road customers with Italian Vignale coachwork. Its production-road programme supported recognition as a manufacturer for the marque’s Le Mans effort. It belongs as an early American high-performance GT with a direct connection to a significant sports-racing programme; the road coupe itself is not credited with the racing cars’ results.
